items.stem: Which statement is a correct double-angle identity for $\cos(2\theta)$?
items.hint: Only one of the four can be reached from $\cos(2\theta)=\cos^{2}\theta-\sin^{2}\theta$ using $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$.

items.stem: Use the sine sum formula to write $\sin\left(x+\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.
items.hint: Expand with $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$, then locate the point on the unit circle at $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ before writing down its cosine and its sine.
worked: The angle $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ sits at the unit-circle point $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, so $\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

items.stem: Angle $A$ lies in Quadrant II with $\sin A=\dfrac{4}{5}$, and angle $B$ lies in Quadrant I with $\sin B=\dfrac{5}{13}$. Find the exact value of $\sin(A+B)$.
items.hint: You are handed both sines, so recover each cosine from $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ and let the quadrant decide the sign of each one.
worked: $A$ is in Quadrant II, where cosine is negative: $\cos A=-\sqrt{1-\dfrac{16}{25}}=-\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{25}}=-\dfrac{3}{5}$.
$B$ is in Quadrant I, where cosine is positive: $\cos B=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{25}{169}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{144}{169}}=\dfrac{12}{13}$.
